candidates.attacker_control: Any remote client fully controls the request's Content-Type header and multipart body. Dispatcher.wrapRequest() only requires the substring "multipart/form-data" (case-sensitive contains()) in the Content-Type to route the request through the multipart parser (Dispatcher.java:791-795); the parser is invoked while the ActionContext/value stack already exists, because createActionContext() runs before wrapRequest() in the filters (StrutsPrepareAndExecuteFilter.java:104-106, StrutsPrepareFilter.java:89-91, StrutsServlet.java:72-75). A boundary/content mismatch (or a non-multipart body containing that substring) makes Commons FileUpload throw an exception whose message embeds the attacker's header value; multipart file names/fields also surface in error messages (JakartaStreamMultiPartRequest.addFileSkippedError builds an exception message containing the client-supplied file name).
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked: (a) the snapshot has a buildErrorMessage()/message-bundle indirection that shows an intended sanitization design — it is a genuine mitigating factor for exception types that have bundle keys, but the fallback path still uses e.getMessage() as message *text*, so the sanitization is incomplete (verified in LocalizedTextUtil.java:723-729). (b) SecurityMemberAccess/OgnlUtil exclude java.lang., ognl, javax and classes such as Runtime/ProcessBuilder/ActionContext (struts-default.xml:41-61) — this is a blacklist that the evaluated expression can work around through the context/container objects, so it does not break the chain. (c) The evaluated message is not escaped/HTML-encoded anywhere in this path. (d) The exact Commons FileUpload exception text could not be read in this snapshot (dependency source/binary absent), so the header->message hop rests on documented library behaviour. (e) I could not confirm from source whether this revision predates an upstream hardening of this exact code path, so a partial-mitigation state cannot be excluded.
candidates.impact: Remote code execution in the application server process (attacker-controlled OGNL expression evaluated with framework context, permitting access to the container and runtime APIs), or at minimum arbitrary expression evaluation/state disclosure. This is reachable pre-action-mapping, on default configuration, making it unauthenticated and low-complexity.
candidates.prerequisites: Default configuration only: struts.multipart.parser=jakarta (org/apache/struts2/default.properties:69) and the Struts filter chain in front of the app. No action mapping is needed for the parser to run, because the request is wrapped before action mapping. The attacker's text must land in an exception message (Commons FileUpload echoes the Content-Type in InvalidContentTypeException; attacker-supplied file names appear in size-limit/skip errors). OGNL evaluation is possible because the context/value stack is available when the message is built.
candidates.root_cause: Multipart parse failures are converted into user-visible messages by passing the *raw exception message* as the default message of LocalizedTextUtil.findText (see buildErrorMessage). LocalizedTextUtil then unconditionally runs TextParseUtil.translateVariables(...) over that default text, i.e. anything of the form %{...} or ${...} in it is compiled and executed as an OGNL expression against the action value stack. Because the request's Content-Type / multipart metadata is echoed by Commons FileUpload into its exception messages (e.g. InvalidContentTypeException '...content type header is <value>'), attacker text reaches expression evaluation. The message bundle only defines two generic keys (SizeLimitExceededException, IOException), so for all other exception types the attacker-influenced default-message fallback is used. The framework relies on message *arguments* (safe) in some places but the fallback path puts untrusted text directly into the message *template*.
candidates.title: Multipart upload error path feeds attacker-controlled request data into OGNL evaluation via the localized error message (expression-language injection → potential RCE)
candidates.trace: 1) Request arrives with Content-Type containing 'multipart/form-data' and a crafted/mismatched body. 2) Dispatcher.wrapRequest() (785-798) creates MultiPartRequestWrapper -> JakartaMultiPartRequest.parse() (82-107) -> commons-fileupload ServletFileUpload.parseRequest() throws FileUploadException whose message contains the attacker's header text (dependency commons-fileupload 1.3.1, pom.xml:711-715; library source not in this snapshot). 3) Catch block calls buildErrorMessage(e, ...) (115-119), which forms key 'struts.messages.upload.error.<ExceptionSimpleName>' and calls LocalizedTextUtil.findText(this.getClass(), errorKey, defaultLocale, e.getMessage(), args) — the raw exception message becomes the default message. 4) The key is generally absent: struts-messages.properties defines only SizeLimitExceededException and IOException (34-37), so LocalizedTextUtil.findText falls into the MissingResourceException path -> getDefaultMessage(key, locale, valueStack, args, defaultMessage) (714-737). 5) getDefaultMessage sets message = defaultMessage (723) and then calls TextParseUtil.translateVariables(message, valueStack) (729). 6) TextParseUtil.translateVariables(char[], ...) (154-168) resolves the container's TextParser and calls evaluate(openChars, expression, ognlEval, maxLoopCount); OgnlTextParser.evaluate (46-66) extracts the %{...}/${...} body and calls evaluator.evaluate(var) -> stack.findValue(var) (TextParseUtil 156-164), i.e. the attacker's expression is compiled/executed by OGNL with the action value stack and ActionContext available (the excluded class/package lists in SecurityMemberAccess/OgnlUtil do not stop this path because the context map and container/OgnlUtil objects remain reachable from the evaluated expression). 7) The resulting action error is also propagated to the action via FileUploadInterceptor (257-263).
candidates.unverified: No runtime or build verification was performed (no code execution/tests per instructions), Commons FileUpload 1.3.1 sources are not present in the snapshot so the exception-message content is inferred from the library's documented getBoundary() behaviour, the exploitability depends on the app running the default multipart parser and the value-stack sandbox bypass being usable in this revision, and the index used for navigation provides no data-flow/reachability proof. Treat as a lead requiring confirmation.
candidates.weakness_type: Expression language / OGNL injection from untrusted input (CWE-917), leading to data-to-code execution

coverage_summary: Coverage: reviewed the core dispatcher/filter chain, multipart handling (all three parsers + wrapper), ParametersInterceptor/StaticParametersInterceptor/ActionMappingParametersInteceptor, Ognl/OgnlUtil/SecurityMemberAccess/TextParseUtil/OgnlTextParser, security package checkers, struts-default.xml/default.properties/struts-messages, validator package (incl. URLValidator/EmailValidator), result package (StrutsResultSupport, ServletRedirectResult, StreamResult/JSP tags partially), DebuggingInterceptor, TokenHelper/TokenInterceptor, REST plugin (mapper, invocation, content-type handlers, XStream/Jackson/JsonLib handlers, struts-plugin.xml), JSON plugin (interceptor/JSONUtil/redirect result sampling), convention plugin action-config building, rest-showcase/showcase apps, and top-level poms. The snapshot itself contains no test or view-template files (src/test, .jsp, .ftl are filtered out by the harness), so test-based confirmation was impossible. Not reviewed exhaustively: plugins/embeddedjsp (vendored Tomcat Jasper), portlet/portlet-tiles/tiles/spring/osgi/sitemesh/jasperreports/jfreechart/gxp/oval/cdi/dwr/testng/plexus/junit internals, bundles/admin, archetypes, assembly descriptors, and large parts of views/components, so no claim of full-repository coverage is made. Relation-index data were used only for navigation (no data-flow, reachability or exploitability proof); the index reports complete syntactic indexing of the 2644 visible files with no missing files.
limitations: No code execution, build, dependency resolution or dynamic testing was performed, so reachability/exploitability are source-inferred only and nothing is runtime-confirmed.

Third-party library sources (commons-fileupload 1.3.1, XStream 1.4.8, OGNL 3.1.4) are not part of the snapshot; their exact behaviour (exception-message content, gadget availability, sandbox constraints) is inferred from version information and public behaviour, not verified here.

I could not diff against upstream or consult any patch/CVE/ground-truth data, so I cannot prove whether the multipart error-message code in this snapshot is the pre-fix or a partially hardened revision; the fallback-to-exception-message path is nevertheless present in the source.

The snapshot has no test sources and no view templates, and the P1 relation index is explicitly navigation-only, so gaps in the index are not evidence that an area was reviewed and no area should be treated as proven clean.
Parts of the tree (notably the vendored Jasper code in plugins/embeddedjsp, portlet/tiles/spring/osgi plugins, bundles and archetypes) were not reviewed in depth.

rejected_leads.lead: REST plugin deserializes untrusted XML with an unrestricted XStream (plugins/rest/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/rest/handler/XStreamHandler.java:43-50, createXStream() returns new XStream(); reachable via ContentTypeInterceptor.java:52-66 with Content-Type application/xml, handler registered by default in plugins/rest/src/main/resources/struts-plugin.xml:35 and wired into restDefaultStack at line 96/108; dependency pinned to xstream 1.4.8 in pom.xml:892-896).
rejected_leads.reason: This is a real high-severity unsafe-deserialization pattern (S2-052/CVE-2017-9805 class) and a very plausible alternative root cause, but it is not a source-only code defect of the same confidence: the risk is dominated by the pinned library version (the fix upstream was a library upgrade/security-framework enablement), and exploitation depends on gadget availability on the classpath. It is recorded as an unconfirmed lead, not the selected candidate, because the one-candidate cap requires choosing the single strongest in-repo code path.

rejected_leads.lead: URLValidator compiles and matches a complex user-supplied regex against attacker-controlled field values with no length guard (core/src/main/java/com/opensymphony/xwork2/validator/validators/URLValidator.java:48-90).
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible catastrophic-backtracking/ReDoS impact, but the impact is availability only, it requires an application to use the url validator on a request-bound field, and I could not verify the backtracking behaviour without executing the regex (execution not permitted).

rejected_leads.lead: DefaultActionMapper takes the namespace directly from the request URI when alwaysSelectFullNamespace is true, with no validation against configured namespaces (core/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/dispatcher/mapper/DefaultActionMapper.java:324-376).
rejected_leads.reason: S2-057-style namespace/OGNL concern, but it only applies when struts.mapper.alwaysSelectFullNamespace is enabled (default false in default.properties:205) and I could not demonstrate an in-snapshot sink that turns the namespace into expression evaluation.

rejected_leads.lead: JSONActionRedirectResult writes the computed redirect location into a JSON response body without escaping (plugins/json/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/json/JSONActionRedirectResult.java:52-61).
rejected_leads.reason: Requires an application whose redirect location incorporates request-derived values, plus the struts.enableJSONValidation/validateOnly parameters to force the JSON response; impact is response/injection class (XSS/JSON splitting) and config-dependent, so it is weaker than the selected candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: apps/showcase FileDownloadAction only rejects inputPath values containing 'WEB-INF' (apps/showcase/.../filedownload/FileDownloadAction.java:41-63).
rejected_leads.reason: Demo application code whose comment documents the deliberately minimal sanitization; ServletContext.getResourceAsStream is confined to the web application root and the sensitive WEB-INF prefix is blocked, so no concrete security impact is established.

rejected_leads.lead: plugins/sitegraph/SiteGraph.render() builds a shell command string with Runtime.getRuntime().exec (plugins/sitegraph/.../SiteGraph.java:133-139).
rejected_leads.reason: The 'output' value comes from the tool's own command-line arguments (Main/getArg), i.e. a developer-supplied build-time input, not an HTTP-reachable attacker-controlled value; not a defensible remote vulnerability.

rejected_leads.lead: RestActionMapper sets the action method from the URI path segment without checking allowDynamicMethodCalls (plugins/rest/.../RestActionMapper.java:221-234, 307-328).
rejected_leads.reason: The value is constrained by strict method invocation (ActionConfig.isAllowedMethod checked in DefaultActionProxy.prepare():195-201) and DMI is disabled by default, so the impact reduces to invoking methods the developer already allowed; no clear access-control bypass could be evidenced from source.

summary: Review of the Struts 2.5-SNAPSHOT tree (2644 model-visible files; tests and view templates are filtered out of the snapshot). I traced input handling in the core dispatcher, multipart handling, interceptor/Ognl/security packages, plus the REST and JSON plugins, configs and poms. The single strongest issue found is a data-to-code path in multipart error handling: attacker-influenced text from a malformed multipart request (exception message containing the request Content-Type / multipart metadata) is placed as the *default message* into LocalizedTextUtil, which evaluates ${}/%{} in that text against the OGNL value stack — the classic Struts remote-code-execution pattern (S2-045/S2-046 class, CWE-917). No runtime verification was performed and no dependency jars are readable in this snapshot; the finding is a lead, not a confirmed vulnerability.
